visHint.hillshade: One light source. Drag the azimuth to sweep it — features running parallel to the light are invisible.
visHint.multiHillshade: Six light directions weighted toward the north-west. No orientation is left unlit.
visHint.vat: RVT's “VAT – Archaeological” recipe: hillshade, slope, positive openness and sky-view factor blended into one greyscale image. Fixed light and fixed contrast limits, so two VAT renders of different places mean the same thing.
visHint.svf: How much of the sky is visible. Independent of light direction: hollows and ditches go dark, mounds and banks go bright.
visHint.openPos: Mean angle up to the horizon in sixteen directions. Independent of light direction like sky-view factor, but it brings out what stands proud: mounds, edges and ridges.
visHint.openNeg: The same measured downwards, as if the terrain were inverted. Drawn on a reversed grey ramp, like slope and sky-view factor, so what cuts in goes dark: ditches, charcoal pits and sunken roads.
visHint.lrm: The elevation model minus a smoothed copy. Removes the landform trend and leaves the small scale standing.
visHint.slope: Steepness of the terrain. Steep is dark.

visGroup.vat: Several measures blended into one picture.
visGroup.svf: No light source — the same picture wherever the sun is.
